title: Catalog Launch & Release Sync Runbook for New Model Additions
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Purpose: A compact operational runbook and checklist to coordinate adding a new model to the public catalog. This doc covers launch readiness across catalog metadata, benchmarks, docs/quickstarts, release notes, marketing sync, and cross-team sign-offs.

Checklist (high-level):
- [ ] Catalog entry: model name, family, architecture, quantization options, tags (use-case, safety), supported APIs, recommended endpoint(s), example cost/latency estimate. Include model card link.
- [ ] Benchmarks: publish p50/p95 latency (default and long context), throughput at reserved sizes (dedicated), tokens/sec for common sequence length buckets (32/128/512). Attach perf dashboard link and raw results.
- [ ] Quality evals: seed prompts, pass/fail thresholds, comparison vs baseline model, and aggregated metrics for hallucination/accuracy/ROUGE/F1 as applicable.
- [ ] SDK/docs: quickstart snippets (Python/JS), streaming example, function-calling sample, and structured-output example. Docs must include supported parameters and migration notes if API behavior differs from defaults.
- [ ] Release notes: single-paragraph summary for Product Release Notes, bullet list of key changes for changelog, migration guidance for customers, and security notice if any.
- [ ] Marketing & comms: blog draft, social assets, Tweet thread, community post; coordinate timing with PR/infra rollout.
- [ ] Legal & security sign-off: confirm model licensing, data usage constraints, PII considerations, and KMS/HSM compatibility if private deployment supported.
- [ ] Sales & support enablement: training doc, FAQ, one-pager for Sales, and support playbook for common triage steps.
- [ ] Rollout plan: canary cohort, soft launch (beta), and full public availability date. Define automatic fallback model(s) and scaling knobs.
- [ ] Monitoring & alerts: baseline SLOs, target p50/p95, token-cost drift alerts, quality regression alerts tied to eval tests, and dashboard links.
- [ ] Rollback criteria: define thresholds (e.g., >15% p95 latency regression, cost >20% above estimate, or >5% drop in quality metrics) and owner for rollback decision.

Task owners and primary contacts:
- PM (launch lead): Liam O'Connell — overall coordination, release notes, comms calendar.
- Eng (perf + infra): Priya Nair — benchmark runs, canary rollout, autoscale tuning (ENG-3122).
- Eng (runtime stability): Marco Silva — KV cache behavior checks, kernel selection validation.
- Design: Noor Patel — doc screenshots, sample UX for console.
- Research/Applied ML: Chen Wu — quality eval review and baseline comparisons.
- Legal & Security: Hannah Brooks — license & privacy sign-off.
- Sales Enablement: Omar Reyes — one-pager and playbook.

Release notes coordination template (for publishing teams):
- Title: New model: <ModelName> — optimized for <use-case>
- TL;DR (1 sentence): What it does and when available.
- Key metrics: latency p50/p95, tokens/sec at recommended instance, cost estimate per 1k tokens.
- Compatibility notes: API differences, parameter defaults that changed, supported SDK versions.
- Migration guidance: short steps for customers to switch endpoints, sample request/response.
- Links: model card, perf dashboard, docs, and GH PRs (examples: https://github.com/redwood-inference/models/pull/2345).

Staging & verification steps before publish:
1) Finalize model card and metadata in the catalog staging table.
2) Run the smoke test suite (quick prompts for basic correctness) and attach logs.
3) Run full perf benchmark and compare vs baseline within allowed tolerance.
4) Docs review and accessibility check.
5) Legal security review completed and logged (ticket in compliance tracker).
6) Support playbook reviewed with at least two support engineers.
7) Marketing assets approved and scheduled.

Communication cadence & channels:
- Weekly launch sync (PM + Eng + Design + Research) — standing invite: Tuesdays 11:00 PT.
- Slack channel: #pm-model-launches (use thread per model).
- Pre-release sign-off: 48 hours before soft launch — final go/no-go email to execs and GTM leads.

Post-launch monitoring & follow-ups:
- Day-0 (first 24h): monitor latency p95/p99, error rate, and cost. Prepare first 24h report.
- 72h: assess usage patterns and early customer feedback; run additional evals on live traffic samples (anonymized).
- 30 days: collect quality/regression metrics and recommend next action: broaden rollout, change defaults, or rollback.

Artifacts & links (placeholders to update):
- Model card (drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/models/<ModelName>-card
- Perf dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/perf/<ModelName>
- Docs PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/678
- GH model onboarding PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/models/pull/2345

Notes and edge decisions made so far:
- Decided to expose quantized variant as "q4_0" default for hosted due to cost targets; dedicated recommended variant remains "fp16" for latency-sensitive customers.
- Agreed to include a short migration note for older SDKs that used a different sampling default; engineering to add a compatibility wrapper.
- Canary cohort will be internal + strategic customers flagged by Account Execs (Sales) for first 72h.

- [Hannah] Confirm license text and any export controls (due 2026-03-16).
